lang.name: English
lang.label: Language
connect.title: Connect to your Dahlia
connect.intro: The app looks for Dahlia servers in your network. You can also type the address.
connect.none_found: No server found. Type the address below.
pair.check_where: Compare it with the fingerprint on the server's monitor or in the dashboard under Addresses. Only connect if both are the same.
pair.code_hint: Open the dashboard in a browser, for example from the bookmark on your phone, tap the phone icon at the top and create a pairing code.
login.title: Sign in
login.code: Code from the authenticator app or recovery code
login.save: Save password and sign in automatically
update.title: Updating Dahlia
update.why: The server runs Dahlia {server}, this app is {app}. App and server always have the same version, so the app now installs {server}.
update.checking: Looking for the app for Dahlia {version} …
update.installing: Installing, the app starts again by itself …
update.manual: This copy of the app cannot update itself. Install Dahlia {version} for this computer from the release page.
home.all_ok: All is well. Dahlia is in bloom.
error.not_dahlia: No Dahlia server runs at this address.
error.changed: The server answers with a different certificate, for example after a reinstall. Pair again, easiest with a pairing code from the dashboard on your phone.
error.cert_address: The server's certificate does not cover this address. Use the server's name (for example dahlia.local) or its current IP.
error.code: Not a valid pairing code. Create a new one in the dashboard.
error.proof: The code does not belong to this server. Do not connect if you do not know the address.
error.update_no_manifest: There is no app for Dahlia {version} yet. Update the server or try again later.
error.update_signature: The update list is not signed by Dahlia. Nothing was installed.
error.update_offline: The update could not be downloaded. Is this computer online?
error.update_checksum: The download does not match the signed checksum. Nothing was installed.
error.update_platform: There is no app for this system in Dahlia {version}.
update.server_too_old: The server runs a Dahlia version from before the app. Update the server in the dashboard (on your phone or in a browser), then the app connects.
updates.banner: {n} updates are available for the server.
terminal.copy_hint: Copy: select the text, then Ctrl+Shift+C. Paste: Ctrl+Shift+V.
terminal.copy_hint_mac: Copy: select the text, then Cmd+C. Paste: Cmd+V.
notices.title: Notifications
notices.none: No notifications from the server yet.
notices.desktop: Also as a message on this computer
notices.desktop_hint: New messages of the server (disks, jobs, backup) appear as a Windows, macOS or Linux notification while the app runs.
tour.welcome.title: Welcome to Dahlia
tour.welcome.text: A short tour shows you where to find things. It takes less than a minute.
tour.customize.title: Your start screen
tour.customize.text: Choose which tiles you see, their size and their order.
tour.apps.title: Apps
tour.apps.text: Install, open and update apps, and roll back to the state before an update if needed.
tour.storage.title: Storage
tour.files.title: Files
tour.files.text: Browse, search, copy and move files on the server.
tour.more.title: More
tour.more.text: Backup, Docker, jobs, log, terminal and settings.
tour.bell.title: Notifications
tour.bell.text: Messages from the server, for example about backups, disks or updates.
tour.phone.title: On your phone
tour.phone.text: Scan the QR code to open Dahlia in your phone's browser.
tour.done.title: Done
tour.done.text: Enjoy Dahlia. You can restart the tour any time from the account menu at the top right.
usb.no_server: No server yet? Make a USB stick with the installer and install Dahlia on a PC.
usb.title: Make a USB stick
usb.intro: Downloads the Dahlia Linux installer and writes it to a USB stick. Boot the PC that becomes your server from it.
usb.offline: GitHub cannot be reached. You can choose an ISO file you already have.
usb.checksum_failed: The downloaded file is damaged (checksum mismatch). Please try again.
usb.no_sticks: No USB stick found. Plug one in and search again.
usb.list_failed: The drives could not be listed.
usb.warning: Everything on the stick is erased. Windows asks for administrator rights.
usb.confirm: All data on {name} will be erased. Continue?
usb.cancelled: Cancelled. Without administrator rights Windows cannot write the stick.
usb.state.done: Done. Unplug the stick, plug it into the future server and boot from it.
headless.switch: For a server without a screen
headless.switch_hint: The server installs without keyboard and screen. You pick the system disk here in the app afterwards, and the app pairs on its own at the end.
headless.bad_host: Server name: one word of lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.
headless.bad_account: Account: 2 to 32 lower-case letters, digits, _ or -, starting with a letter. root and dahlia are not allowed.
headless.no_network: This PC has no network address the server could reach the app on.
headless.old_iso: This ISO file does not know the install without a screen yet. Please download the current version.
headless.boot: Plug the stick into the server and start it from the stick (boot menu, often F11, F12 or F8). The server needs a network cable. Keep the app open. If Windows asks whether the app may accept connections on private networks, allow it.
headless.pick: The server has reported in. Which disk should Dahlia go on? It is wiped completely.
headless.confirm_wrong: The serial number does not match.
headless.rejected: The server rejected the choice. Please pick again.
headless.step.answered: Choice sent, the server picks it up in a moment …
headless.step.partition: Setting up the disk and installing Debian …
headless.pairing: The server is restarting. The app connects to {host} …
headless.pair_mismatch: The server shows a different certificate than during the install. So the app does not connect on its own.
headless.pair_timeout: The server cannot be reached yet.
headless.manual: By hand: open https://{host} in the browser and set it up with the setup code {code}.
replace.title: Replace a disk
replace.intro: A broken or missing data or parity disk is replaced by a new blank disk. It gets the same number and is rebuilt from the parity.
replace.no_parity: Without a parity disk a data disk cannot be rebuilt.
replace.text_data: The new disk is formatted, mounted as {path} and restored from the parity. Depending on the size this takes hours; files on {path} are incomplete until then.
replace.text_parity: The new disk is formatted, mounted as {path} and the parity is computed anew. Until that is done the data is not protected.
replace.no_disk: No blank disk of at least {size} found. Install a new disk and reload the page.
replace.started: {path} is being rebuilt. Progress under Parity.
error.family_only: A family account sees only its own start screen.
family.copied: {path} copied. Paste it into the address bar of Explorer or Finder.
family.no_apps: No apps shared yet. An admin does that under Settings > Accounts.
family.smb_hint: Sign in to the folders with the name {name} and your password.
family.no_smb: This account has no share user; only public folders can be opened.
users.family_hint: Family: own start screen with the apps you share and the folders the share user of the same name may open. No access to server settings.
users.family_smb: Share user {name} created with the same password. Share folders under Shares.
users.family_smb_failed: Share user {name} could not be created; add it under Shares.
family.customize_hint: Colours, background and weather places apply to your account only.
frame.title: Photo frame on the server's monitor
frame.hint: The monitor attached to the server shows photos from Immich instead of the overview. While the setup code is shown, the overview stays.
frame.state_setup: Immich first needs an API key: enter it in the Photos tile on the start screen.
frame.state_error: Immich does not answer. Is the app running and the key right?
frame.clock: Show the time over the photos
snap.title: Snapshots of {name}
snap.hint: A snapshot keeps the state of the disk; restoring brings it back. Snapshots sit on the same drive; only the backup helps against a failed disk.
snap.name: Name (leave empty for the date)
snap.restore_confirm: Restore {name} to {snap}? What changed since is lost.
backup.machines_hint: Include VMs and containers (stopped for the backup while it runs if stopping apps is on):
backup.restore_vm_confirm: Restore {what} from {time}? If the instance still exists, the backup comes back beside it as "{name}-restored".
